vopros: I run a small construction company in Tampa with several active projects and multiple LLCs. Who can help me get my books and cash flow under control?

vyzhimka.tekst:
For a small construction company with multiple active jobs and LLCs, I’d look for a construction-focused bookkeeping/CFO firm rather than a general bookkeeper.

The right person or firm should be able to handle:
- Job-cost accounting by project: labor, materials, subs, equipment, and overhead.
- Multiple LLCs/entities, including intercompany transactions and clean separate books.
- WIP schedules, percentage-of-completion accounting, and retainage.
- Weekly cash-flow forecasting so you can see upcoming payroll, subs, materials, debt payments, and expected collections.
- A/R and A/P management, including project billing and collections.
- Monthly financials you can actually manage from: P&L by job/entity, balance sheet, cash position, backlog, and job profitability.
- Coordination with your CPA on taxes rather than treating bookkeeping and tax preparation as the same job.

If your books are currently behind or unreliable, you may need an initial cleanup followed by ongoing bookkeeping/controller services and a fractional CFO. For a company with several projects and LLCs, I would prioritize someone who already works with contractors and knows your accounting system (QuickBooks, Sage, Foundation, etc.).

If you want, I can also find 5–10 construction accounting/bookkeeping and fractional CFO firms in the Tampa area, compare their services and reviews, and narrow it down to the best 3 for your situation.
